authorized_by: Study owner instruction, 2026-11-02: native macOS arm64 llama.cpp b12020, explicitly CPU-only, four threads, one slot; tools and grading in a Linux container.
reason: The v1.1 execution host (Linux x86_64 Codex sandbox) is unavailable. Restoration host is an Apple M5 (arm64) Mac. The pinned ubuntu-x64 llama-server runs under Rosetta at 7 prompt tok/s and 4.5 generated tok/s; a synthetic ~3,000-token prompt did not finish within 900 s, versus about 80 s for a comparable 2,733-token prompt in the original traces. Under Rosetta nearly every episode would end at the 20-minute wall budget, so episodes would measure emulation overhead, not the model.
changes: Inference runtime: llama.cpp tag b12020 (commit 0ec4027a2a0183de87c007069adddc06e665f7de) built from the GitHub tag source archive on macOS arm64 with GGML_METAL=OFF, GGML_BLAS=OFF, GGML_ACCELERATE=OFF, GGML_RPC=OFF, static. No GPU/accelerator device exists in the binary (--list-devices: none). The official macos-arm64 release binary was rejected because it links Metal and Accelerate/BLAS, which llama.cpp attaches even with --device none.

Server arguments: identical to the frozen agent_calibration.start_server arguments (same model file, -c 32768 -t 4 -tb 4 --parallel 1 --reasoning-budget 128 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18090 --no-ui) plus --device none -ngl 0. Launched on the host by amendment_1.2/start_native_server.sh under caffeinate.

Agent tools and independent grading: Ubuntu 24.04 linux/amd64 container (glibc 2.39, Python 3.12.14, uv 0.13.4, Node v24.22.1, npm 11.9.0, GCC 13.3) under Rosetta in a Lima vz VM; defined by amendment_1.2/Dockerfile. The project is bind-mounted at the original /workspace/scratch/93af20bbcd93/packaging_study path, so frozen provenance paths resolve unchanged.
Endpoint: the frozen endpoint http://127.0.0.1:18090 inside the container is a byte-level TCP relay (amendment_1.2/endpoint_forwarder.py) to the host server.

Controller: amendment_1.2/run_batch_native.py runs the unmodified run_batch.main, replacing only start_server with an attach-and-verify function (model path, one slot, 32768 context) that leaves the host server running.
Checkpoint zip location ROOT.parent is mapped to restoration_1.2/checkpoint_parent on the host disk so per-episode checkpoints persist.

Moved unchanged to pilots/v1.1-interrupted/00-pyfiglet-154-A-19 (calls.json sha256 be095bdbd5030c103dad1469d31d74c3defb0e5b2436064539b73e9a3d9ff6ba). The status file's '2 responses' was the last 15-second status tick.
replacement.reason: Host lost before any outcome; run_study.episode refuses to overwrite an existing episode directory. The episode restarts from a fresh workspace with the same seed, condition and order. Its partial trajectory (commands and timings only) was inspected during restoration; no repair outcome exists.

known_differences_and_threats: Hardware speed: native CPU inference is faster than the original host (synthetic: ~88-102 prompt tok/s, ~20 decode tok/s in llama-bench; ~16 generated tok/s end-to-end through the runner, versus about 3-9 end-to-end in original traces). The 8,192-token budget will usually bind before the 20-minute wall budget, which is a different budget mix than on the original host. Both conditions are equally affected.
arm64 ggml kernels differ numerically from x86_64 kernels, so seeded generations will not reproduce original token streams. The v1.0/v1.1 partial traces are not comparable.

Agent and grader run x86_64 code under Rosetta translation; kernel 7.0.0 versus recorded 6.18.57. All 24 affected/reference controls reproduce the frozen P/F matrix online and offline in this environment, and both preflights pass.
Agent PATH and HOME differ from the Codex sandbox (/opt/codex paths absent). UV_PYTHON points to the container's Python 3.12.14.
Fanless MacBook Air: sustained thermal throttling may slow later episodes. Per-call timings are retained in every trajectory.

The source-built binary reports build_info b0-unknown (archive lacks git metadata). Identity rests on the tag-to-commit mapping, the source archive hash and the binary hash in amendment_1.2/FREEZE_1.2.json.
